name: Sloth (acedia) as capital vice
plainSummary: In this list, sloth is not mere laziness: it is spiritual apathy—refusal of the good one owes, especially toward God and neighbor.
description: Derived principle: acedia (sloth) is the capital vice of spiritual torpor or sorrow at the demands of the good—classically distinct from clinical depression, though the two raise difficult pastoral and medical questions.
foundationStrengthRationale: Rich in monastic literature; modern readers often confuse acedia with laziness or depression, requiring careful interpretation.

pros.claim: Names civic and relational failure when people withdraw from obligations they could meet.
pros.evidence: Parallel discussions exist in virtue ethics (effort, diligence) and organizational ethics (negligence).

cons.claim: Moral language of sloth can blame victims of depression, burnout, or structural barriers.
cons.evidence: Mental health and disability advocates caution against spiritualizing illness or exhaustion.
